stem:
Sneha pours water into two glass tumblers that are the same shape and size. Tumbler P has water up to a higher mark than tumbler Q.

Which conclusion about volume is correct?

options.text: Tumbler P contains a larger volume of water because the water occupies more space.
Both tumblers contain equal volumes of water because they have the same capacity.
A tall narrow bottle with a higher water level than P must hold more water than P, even though it is much thinner.
Tumbler Q holds more water than P because more empty space remains above its lower water level.

teacher.key_rationale: In identical containers, higher water level means larger occupied volume. Capacity is not the same as the volume currently held; level comparisons need matching width; lower level does not mean more water.
